title: Chicken Little, or Henny-Penny
note: A concise reading adaptation faithful to Joseph Jacobs’s public-domain “Henny-Penny.” The opening and recurring dialogue retain Jacobs’s wording; cumulative passages are compressed, and page divisions are editorial. “Chicken Little” is included in the display title as the familiar American name for the tale.

rights.basis: Project Gutenberg identifies ebook 7439 as public domain in the United States.

artLabel: Henny-Penny hurries from the farmyard beneath a wide and harmless sky.

pageArt.alt: Henny-Penny leads Cocky-locky, Ducky-daddles, Goosey-poosey, and Turkey-lurkey toward the distant castle.
Foxy-woxy offers to guide the five birds toward the king.
Henny-Penny runs safely home from the mouth of Foxy-woxy’s dark cave.

scenes: One day Henny-penny was picking up corn in the cornyard when—whack!—something hit her upon the head. “Goodness gracious me!” said Henny-penny; “the sky’s a-going to fall; I must go and tell the king.”

So she went along and she went along and she went along till she met Cocky-locky. “Where are you going, Henny-penny?” says Cocky-locky. “Oh! I’m going to tell the king the sky’s a-falling,” says Henny-penny. “May I come with you?” says Cocky-locky. “Certainly,” says Henny-penny.

They went along till they met Ducky-daddles, then Goosey-poosey, and then Turkey-lurkey. Each asked where they were going; each heard that the sky was falling; and each joined the company going to tell the king.

So they went along till they met Foxy-woxy. When the birds told him their errand, Foxy-woxy said: “Oh! but this is not the way to the king. I know the proper way; shall I show it you?” They all agreed, and followed him.

They came to a narrow and dark hole, the door of Foxy-woxy’s cave. Foxy-woxy called it the short way to the king’s palace and went in first. Turkey-lurkey followed, then Goosey-poosey and Ducky-daddles; and Foxy-woxy snapped off each one’s head. Cocky-locky went next, but Foxy-woxy’s first bite only hurt him, and Cocky-locky called out to Henny-penny.
So she turned tail and ran back home, so she never told the king the sky was a-falling.
